notes.title: New Year Update.
notes.notes: Few fixes. But the main one is the light baking system.

notes.title: Specular reflections.
notes.notes:
More improvements/fixes in the custom Rendering Pipeline. 
There might be more level design bugs than before: missing objects, and mashes.

notes.title: FPV & Specular Lights
notes.notes:
[h2]Specular environment reflections[/h2]
The lighting engine has been altered dramatically. Specular reflections now have the correct glossiness. This also introduced a few artefacts, none of which are a mystery and will be fixed soon. Sometimes, upon entering the area, it may have incorrect light—I have disabled light cleanup for some scenarios, but in some, it is necessary.

[h2]FPV simulator[/h2]
It now has an FPV mode. As the name suggests - it is a small level where you can fly around. In the future, FPV will be a part of Turret Defence mode. To have the player something to do while the monsters are walking.

[h2]Cleanup[/h2]
Few third-party assets have been removed from the build - hence the smaller build size. A more noticeable one is the water system. It was causing a bit too many issues. I'll return to making a good water solution or integrating the existing one.

notes.title: A few follow-up fixes.
notes.notes:
* Fixed Fog aliasing
* Added limited Gamepad support (Tower defence part still needs keyboard & mouse)

There is still a weird bug that makes fog brighter in the build. Maybe some colourspace conversion inconsistency somewhere.
Will figure it out one day.

notes.title: Shaders and effects
notes.notes:
This update contains lots of visual changes. 
[list]
[*] New Custom Volumetric Fog System.
[*] Custom RayTracing and baking use more optimized spacial partition.
[*] Added Zibra's smoke simulation with a custom shader to interact with baked light.
[*] And lots of small stuff.
[/list]

There are more things in the works: cutscenes, monsters that hide in shadows, and space exploration.

Overall, the plan is to start crafting a real narrative experience: characters, animations, dialogues, cinematics. Levels will be redone from their Boxy primitives into something more realistic. Those are skills I'm not super proficient in, so at the current stage, I do more experiments with graphics while searching for collaborators. 
There is a cool sound effects guy from Norway, ready to assist.
My good friend Jai from [b]Nexus XIII[/b] band is there to land more tracks and help with writing and voicing.
We still need a cool animator though.
And then a nice, not super long, but mind-twisting experience will be born.
